header.name: Quentin Lopes
header.subtitle: Game Developer • Unreal Engine / C++ • Unity / C# • Music Composer
about.title: About Me
about.text:
Game Development student specialized in Game Programming, with a strong focus on C++, Unreal Engine and Blueprints, C# and Unity.

I am particularly interested in character and camera systems to find the better feeling I can in my projetcs.
That's why I want to become a Game Programmer specialized in 3C systems !
I also work on music composition and sound design, as I believe audio plays a critical role in player experience.

I enjoy understanding how to make the best game feeling for different situations and games.
firstYear.title: First Year Projects
firstYear.sywar.desc:
Individual Project - Turn-based combat system featuring clickable areas to choose various actions. Built in C++ with SFML over the course of one week.
This is my first gaming project in Gaming Campus. I had never really code before, I've learn all the bases of coding with this project.

The code in it is ugly, all the code is in one file main with so mush mistakes. I keep it like that to remember where I come from to see my progression and be proud on myself !
firstYear.zaun.desc: Shoot’em up featuring a wave system that spawns enemies in predefined patterns, ending with a final boss fight inspired by Arcane – League of Legends. Developed in C++ using SFML over a two‑week period.
firstYear.zeldo.desc: Collaborative three‑person project centered on developing player mechanics and a map‑generation system driven by .txt file parsing. Completed in two weeks.
firstYear.detective.desc:
Individual Project - Point & Click game developed on a custom engine by Sylvain Seccia (Seccia.dev). Due to the absence of dedicated artists, the environment visuals were produced using AI‑generated assets.
With this project I've discovered the aspect of working on a custom engine. It gives me the occasion to had different approach to produce a game with the constraints imposed.
firstYear.kathos.desc:
Team Project - Large‑scale team project where I acted as Lead Tech, coordinating 4 programmers, 2 artists, and 2 business students. Built in C++ with SFML within a three‑week timeframe.
This project gave me the opportunity to work with a large team, it developed my organisation, my communication and my patience... It developed my capacity to read clearly the code of my mates and correct them when it was necessary.
secondYear.title: Second Year Projects
secondYear.mathlib.desc: A custom mathematics library written in C++ and completed within two weeks.
secondYear.pink.desc:
Team Project - Runner game focused on player physics and 3C.
Pink Paradox was my first second-year project, designed as a refresher of the concepts learned during the first year.
In a team of 3 programmers, we had to create a Runner while focusing on the 3C principles (Character, Camera, Controller).
The objective was to create smooth and enjoyable gameplay, supported by a procedurally generated environment that evolves according to the player's speed.
secondYear.blender.desc:
Introduction to artistic vocabulary and foundational 3D concepts using Blender, aimed at improving collaboration with artists. Completed in two weeks.
I don't have an artist soul but this project was fun to do ^^
secondYear.arena.desc:
Team Project - A large‑scale collaborative project bringing together G‑Art and G‑Tech students, combining artistic and programming expertise. Developed using Unreal Engine 5.6 within a three‑week timeframe.With a team of 3-4, this project was the occasion to work on Unreal Engine (only Blueprints).
I have worked on the character, the shoot system, the boss, the sound design, the music and all the map design (place holder for artists).
secondYear.multi.desc: Discovery and practical implementation of multiplayer systems in Unreal Engine 5.6, focusing on replication. Completed within two weeks.
secondYear.engine.desc: Custom Game Engine real time. Released in C++ in 4 weeks.
secondYear.casino.desc:
Game Jam Project - Made with a team of 19 persons (12 G-Tech and 7 G-Art) with Unreal Engine 5.6 in 40h. I've worked on the weapon, musics, sound design and organisation of all the team.
With this Jam, I have discovered what reel team organisation was : Communication on all the task or features you worked on or add to the project. Push & Merge Git synchronisation, communication with artist to know there work and add their creation to the project progressively.
secondYear.intern.desc:
Large‑scale Metaverse project, where I contributed to the creation and customization of vehicles in Earniverse, including boats, hoverboards, and horses.
That was a really interesting internship for project organisation. If your project have no folder architecture, its hard to work in it. Now, I keep better attention to my folders in my projects.
This experience allowed me to discover remote work. As I am used to working from home, adapting to this environment was not an issue.
thirdYear.unity.desc:
Project focused on Unity fundamentals and 3C systems for both vehicles and character.
The project requirements were fairly simple, so I decided to go beyond the initial scope by creating a complete environment to give the project a more polished and professional look.
My main goal was to create the best possible camera experience for the player and deliver strong game feel through responsive controls and smooth interactions.
I really enjoyed working on this project. At the time, I was not yet certain about the type of developer I wanted to become.
Thanks to this project, I realized that I want to pursue a career as a Gameplay Programmer, ideally specializing in 3C systems (Character, Camera & Controller).
thirdYear.bouclette.desc:
Bouclette is a Game Jam project made during the CStudio Event in 46 Hours on Unreal Engine 5.7.
That was my first Game Jam outside the Gaming Campus with Ubisoft, MadBox and Voodoo that represented the jury.
A reel challenge because we were two programmers and one artist. That was a great experience because we had the opportunity to confront our skills to other persons and we win the price of Originality !
